meta.title: Implement pagination for posts, admin sections and search
meta.body_summary: Add pagination across FlaskBlog views (index, category, search, admin panels, dashboard) with reusable helper and pagination macro.

perf_labels.notes: OpenAI_Codex added pagination across views; no review, maintainer self-merged; no performance evidence.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: Small-to-medium change (380 lines across 15 files) adding pagination feature; fits a low-risk feature PR that was self-merged without review, which is consistent with the successful merge.

review_details.concern_detail: No formal review or comments present.
review_details.performance_claim: Pagination improves page load by limiting results per page, but no explicit quantitative claim in body.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Feature addition without review or evidence; maintainer (same user) merged immediately, suggesting low process friction for self-authored PRs.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark or performance data; only testing commands (ruff, pytest) but no performance verification.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No review feedback or regression observed.

core_change_summary.description: Added pagination to multiple Flask routes using a reusable paginate utility and a Jinja pagination macro. Routes like index, category, search, admin panels, and dashboard now accept page parameter and limit results.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Template adjustments to include pagination macro.
change_trajectory: First commit: Added pagination logic in each route individually, plus template pagination component.
Second commit: Refactored pagination into a shared helper function in app/utils/paginate.py, reducing per-route code.

collaboration_trajectory: PR created by DogukanUrker with two commits from OpenAI_Codex (committed under DogukanUrker).
No external reviews or comments; merged by same user ~7.7 hours after creation.
